claims.title: Inference requests may be readable on the public-to-gateway path if transport encryption is absent
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request` is not present, an on-path attacker between `entity:calling-service` and the internet-facing `process:inference-gateway` can intercept inference requests containing end-user text and PII. The flow crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:serving-edge`; captured prompts can reveal user-supplied information and help target the calling teams' users.

quotes.text: That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unknown transport-encryption state, because `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request` crosses the public-internet boundary to an internet-facing service. Impact is medium because intercepted requests can contain end-user text and PII, but the model does not establish corpus-scale disclosure from one captured request.

mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request` to TLS 1.2+ and validate the gateway certificate; use mTLS where calling-service identities can support it.
Avoid placing unnecessary identifiers or sensitive fields in inference requests, and use opaque references where the gateway can resolve needed context.

claims.title: Gateway-to-model requests may be exposed across the serving-edge boundary
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` remains unverified on `flow:process:inference-gateway>process:model-server>forward-request`, an attacker able to observe the boundary between `process:inference-gateway` and `process:model-server` can intercept forwarded inference payloads containing PII. This crosses from `boundary:serving-edge` into `boundary:model-network`; captured prompts may disclose user input and supply attacker reconnaissance about model-serving requests.

quotes.text: The gateway forwards the request to the model server, which runs the actual model on GPU nodes in our model network.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium, conditional on the unknown encryption state, because an attacker needs a position on the serving-edge-to-model-network path even though the flow crosses a trust boundary. Impact is medium because the forwarded request carries PII-bearing inference payloads and raw prompts may contain user-supplied content.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the internal inference hop
mitigations.detail: Require mTLS on `flow:process:inference-gateway>process:model-server>forward-request` so requests remain confidential and the unauthenticated gateway-to-model-server hop is replaced with verified service identity.

claims.title: Model artifacts may be readable in transit while the model server loads them
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact`, an attacker observing the model-network path can intercept model artifacts as `process:model-server` retrieves them from `store:model-registry-bucket`. The disclosure can expose proprietary model behavior and artifact contents, enabling later model extraction or targeted attacks against the serving stack.

quotes.text: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low, conditional on the unknown encryption state, because interception requires a foothold on an internal model-network path. Impact is medium because `store:model-registry-bucket` holds business-critical model artifacts whose disclosure can reveal valuable model implementation and behavior.

mitigations.detail: Configure `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact` to use TLS with certificate validation and restrict the model server to the expected object-storage endpoint.

claims.title: Customer features may be exposed on the model-server-to-Redis read path
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features`, an attacker observing the internal Redis connection can intercept per-customer account ages and spend bands. Those PII and financial attributes can be correlated with inference requests handled by `process:model-server`, exposing customer profiles and enabling targeted fraud or privacy attacks.

quotes.text: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium, conditional on the unknown encryption state, because a network foothold in the model network is required but the Redis read path is repeatedly used for requests. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is confidential and holds both `pii` and `financial` customer attributes.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS on `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features`, validate the Redis endpoint, and use authenticated service identity rather than relying on model-network placement.

claims.title: Raw prompts may be exposed while the gateway writes debugging logs
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:inference-gateway>store:inference-log>write-request-log`, an attacker observing that path can intercept raw prompts and model responses sent from `process:inference-gateway` to `store:inference-log`. The captured content may include what end users typed, allowing disclosure beyond the original calling team and expanding the data available for social engineering or targeted privacy abuse.

quotes.text: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging. That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low, conditional on the unknown encryption state, because the logging flow is within the serving-edge zone and requires an internal path-observation foothold. Impact is medium because every logged request and response can contain raw user-entered prompt content and PII.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS with endpoint validation for `flow:process:inference-gateway>store:inference-log>write-request-log`.
Redact or tokenize prompt fields at `process:inference-gateway` and log only the diagnostic fields needed for debugging.

claims.title: Model artifacts may be exposed while engineers publish them to the registry
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:entity:ml-engineer>store:model-registry-bucket>publish-artifact`, an on-path observer can intercept model artifacts as `entity:ml-engineer` publishes them to `store:model-registry-bucket`. Disclosure of artifacts can reveal proprietary model logic and make subsequent attacks against model-serving behavior more effective.

quotes.text: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low, conditional on the unknown encryption state, because an attacker must observe an internal engineer-to-registry path. Impact is medium because the published artifacts are business-critical data and their disclosure can expose proprietary model implementation.

mitigations.detail: Enforce TLS with certificate validation on `flow:entity:ml-engineer>store:model-registry-bucket>publish-artifact` and use a managed artifact-publishing client that refuses plaintext endpoints.

claims.title: A copied Redis volume could disclose customer financial features if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:redis-feature-store` is confidential and contains per-customer account age and spend-band data. If its unknown `encryption_at_rest` state resolves to no encryption, an attacker holding a storage copy, snapshot, backup, or decommissioned volume can read the PII and financial feature corpus without using `process:model-server` or the normal Redis read path. The disclosure can be correlated with requests handled by the model server to profile customers.

quotes.text: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` state because storage copies can bypass application controls, although obtaining one requires storage-layer access. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is classified confidential and tagged `pii` and `financial`.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for Redis
mitigations.detail: Establish the at-rest posture of `store:redis-feature-store`, then require managed-key encryption for its persistent storage, backups, snapshots, and replicas.
Limit snapshot, export, backup, and recovery permissions to dedicated principals and monitor bulk export activity.

claims.title: A copied inference-log dataset could expose raw user prompts if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: If the unknown `encryption_at_rest` state of `store:inference-log` resolves to no encryption, a party obtaining a storage-layer copy can read raw prompts and model responses without invoking `process:inference-gateway`. Because the gateway records every request and response for debugging, one copied dataset can disclose user-entered content from multiple calling teams and support later privacy or social-engineering attacks.

quotes.text: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging. That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` state because a copied log dataset bypasses the application but still requires storage-layer access. Impact is medium because the store retains raw prompts that sometimes contain user-entered content, while its broader data classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Verify encryption for the inference-log dataset and operational copies
mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for `store:inference-log`, including exports, backups, and temporary query-result locations.

mitigations.summary: Apply minimization and retention to prompts
mitigations.detail: Redact sensitive prompt fields before writing to `store:inference-log`, restrict retention, and separate diagnostic metadata from raw content.

claims.title: A copied model-registry store could disclose artifacts if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: If the unknown `encryption_at_rest` state of `store:model-registry-bucket` resolves to no encryption, an attacker who obtains a storage copy can read model artifacts directly rather than authenticating as `process:model-server` or `entity:ml-engineer`. The resulting artifact disclosure can reveal proprietary model behavior and enable more precise attacks against the inference service.

quotes.text: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` state because a storage copy bypasses application access controls but must first be obtained. Impact is medium because the bucket contains business-critical model artifacts, although its data classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce registry-bucket encryption at rest
mitigations.detail: Establish whether `store:model-registry-bucket` is encrypted at rest and require managed-key encryption for the bucket, artifact versions, backups, and exports.
Use separate least-privilege roles for artifact readers, publishers, backup operators, and key users so one storage-copy permission does not expose the registry.

claims.title: A compromised model server can read all registry artifacts available to its service account
claims.description: An attacker running code in `process:model-server` inherits the model server service account used by `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact` and can read artifacts from `store:model-registry-bucket`. This is a disclosure risk if that service-account grant is broader than the specific startup artifact required; stolen artifacts reveal proprietary model behavior and can support subsequent attacks on the serving environment.

quotes.text: It uses its own service account for that.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because exploitation requires code execution in `process:model-server`, whose exposure is unknown rather than established as internet-facing. Impact is medium because the inherited account can disclose business-critical model artifacts from `store:model-registry-bucket`.

mitigations.summary: Scope the model-server identity to the required artifact
mitigations.detail: Grant the `process:model-server` service account read access only to the approved model version or prefix needed at startup, rather than broad bucket listing and read authority.
Use short-lived workload identity, restrict metadata-token access, and isolate the model server so a compromise cannot reuse its registry credentials broadly.

claims.title: Unauthenticated Redis access may expose all customer feature records
claims.description: If the unresolved authentication state on `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` has no mechanism beyond the stated absence of a Redis password, an attacker with code execution in `process:model-server` or another model-network component can query `store:redis-feature-store` directly and read customer account ages and spend bands. The store is described as internal, but internal placement does not protect the data after a model-network foothold; the resulting PII and financial profiles can be correlated with inference activity.

quotes.text: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.
The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unresolved Redis authentication state because an attacker needs a model-network component foothold, but the source states Redis has no password. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is confidential and holds `pii` and `financial` data for customers.

mitigations.detail: Configure a dedicated, rotated Redis credential or workload-identity-backed authentication for `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features`, and deny unauthenticated commands.
Use separate narrowly scoped reader identities, network policy, and application-level customer authorization so a compromised component cannot enumerate the full feature corpus.
Require TLS for Redis client connections so authentication material and customer features are not exposed on the model-network path.
